claim: Obvious or remembered ideas come first; new ideas come later, take longer (8.73 s vs 6.69 s) and recruit more executive regions. Order effect, not only fluency.
agent_test: Log the first k ideas; test whether a forced 'discard the first 3 obvious answers' step raises novelty at equal tokens. Samples were only 24-35, so effect sizes are upper bounds.

claim: Creative generation involves cooperation of default (memory, association) and executive (evaluation) networks that are normally anticorrelated at rest.
schema_part: two phases: loose generation then control
agent_test: Single-pass generate vs generate then separate critic pass at equal tokens on AUT-style tasks. Caveat: mostly N=12-30 studies; the meta-analysis (b11) finds overlap with the semantic control network more than default. Gap search: n=171 replication of default-frontoparietal coupling during divergent thinking (d13); pre-registered IFG-IPL predictor (d14).

claim: Early window couples default with salience (insula), later window with executive (DLPFC): a switch-then-control order.
agent_test: Single study N=25 with five usable windows. Test an explicit 'notice what is salient' step before generation vs none. Gap search: Lloyd-Cox 2022 (d12) finds executive network already above default early, so a salience-then-executive order is not confirmed.

claim: Poetry and design show generation with attenuated executive activity and revision/evaluation with re-engaged executive activity.
schema_part: two phases: loose generation then control
agent_test: Separate generate and revise prompts vs one mixed prompt at equal tokens. a12 was abstract-only.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Whole-brain task connectivity predicts divergent-thinking originality in new people, but effects are small (r 0.13-0.35). The high-creative network generalised to 3 external samples; the low-creative network replicated in only 1 of 3 and did not differ significantly from the high one.
agent_test: Not testable on an agent. Caution: one lab, small r, data reused later (a25).

claim: The number of DMN-ECN switches at rest predicts divergent thinking but not intelligence, with an inverted U for switching balance (N=2433, 10 samples; task fMRI N=31 confirmed).
agent_test: Sweep number of generate/evaluate alternations at equal tokens; expect an inverted U.

claim: Creative achievement can go with MORE separation of control and default networks, not more coupling. Coupling vs separation is not settled.
agent_test: Control-strength sweep: does heavier controller involvement hurt novelty?

claim: Brain-wide association effects are small and underpowered at n about 25, so many network-creativity effects from small samples are likely inflated.
agent_test: Treat all N<50 effect sizes (r=.44, extreme groups n=12) as upper bounds. a24 was abstract-only. Marek 2022 (d15) now read at abstract level: median study n about 25, ~50,000 people in the check.

claim: Lesion evidence: medial PFC (default) damage impairs generating remote concepts; rostrolateral PFC (executive) damage impairs combining them. A generate/combine dissociation.
schema_part: two phases: loose generation then control
agent_test: b04 is review-table level only; b19 has 18 FTD patients. Test separate 'produce remote candidates' and 'combine' steps.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Semantic search in creative people deviates from optimal foraging (slower clustering, faster switching). Behaviour replicated in two samples; the brain-behaviour link was found in one MRI sample only.
agent_test: Force topic switches at fixed intervals in idea generation vs free switching at equal tokens.

claim: In LLMs, stacking constraints trades correctness for divergence; reasoning strategies built for accuracy did little for creativity except tree search.
agent_test: Replicate constraint stacking at equal tokens with and without a selection step.

claim: Generate-then-evaluate scaffolds beat single-pass on tasks with a checkable answer: Tree of Thoughts Game of 24 74% vs CoT 4% (GPT-4); creative writing coherence 7.56 vs 6.93. Bottleneck was generation (GPT-4 gen + GPT-3.5 eval 64%; reverse 31%).
schema_part: two phases: loose generation then control
agent_test: ToT vs best-of-N at equal tokens.

claim: LLM over-generation saturates: about 5% (200 of 4000) ideas were non-duplicates at cosine 0.8. LLM research ideas were rated more novel than experts' (5.64 vs 4.84) but LLM judges rank ideas near chance (best 53.3% vs human reviewers 56.1%).
schema_part: control phase needs an outside check
agent_test: Measure duplicate rate vs sample count; use an executed or retrieved check for ranking instead of self-judging. Gap search: retrieval-planning (Nova, d07) lifts unique ideas 3.4x; self-verification works for checkable proofs (d10) but no repair of novelty judging found.

claim: LLM outputs are homogeneous within and across models (pairwise similarity above 0.8; variability 0.459 vs human 0.738); diversity drops with RLHF and with LLM-assisted human writing.
agent_test: Pairwise similarity of K samples with/without persona or decomposition prompts at equal tokens.

claim: Temperature is a weak creativity lever; prompt structure (task decomposition) raises diversity more.
agent_test: Temperature sweep vs structured prompt at equal tokens. c12 correlation values were not extracted.

claim: A three-phase multi-agent framework (diverge, discuss, converge) raised originality and elaboration over a single agent.
schema_part: two phases: loose generation then control
agent_test: Equal-token comparison against one agent given the same total budget.

claim: LLM representations at the early cue stage align with human DMN (r=0.55 with model size, r=0.52 with AUT score), but the two correlations use different pooling and the AUT one depends on the smallest model (falls to 0.40 without it). Alignment weakens during generation.
agent_test: Correlational over about a dozen models; not design evidence.

claim: No study found that tests a DMN/ECN two-network architecture inside an LLM; the frame is analogy only.
agent_test: Gap. Absence is weak evidence because of search tool failures.

claim: LLMs beat average humans on divergent thinking in most comparisons (Hedges g 0.5-2.6) but top humans still exceed the best LLM outputs, and fluency matching changes the size.
agent_test: Mostly via a secondary review; c18 and c19 not opened.

claim: Flow involves reduced core DMN, more lateral frontoparietal activity and DMN-ECN coupling (nine studies).
agent_test: b13 and c24 are the same review lineage; not independent.

claim: Meta-analysis of divergent-thinking fMRI (20 studies, 596 participants) finds the largest overlap with the semantic control network, not default; an older review of 72 experiments found no reliable changes beyond diffuse prefrontal.
agent_test: Treat 'control' as retrieval control (pick weak associates) rather than generic evaluation; compare the two critic prompts.

claim: Verbalized Sampling (one prompt asking for several answers with probabilities) raises LLM creative diversity 1.6-2.1x with a controlled compute budget; larger models gain more. Gacha Decoding (plan modes, pick with an external RNG) gets the same coverage with 4.7x-11x fewer samples.
agent_test: Compare VS or Gacha-style generation against plain resampling at equal tokens on AUT and NoveltyBench; log tokens. Authors' own evaluations; both preprints.

claim: Typicality bias in human preference data explains part of why LLMs give the obvious answer first, a cognitive-bias parallel to the human 'remembered ideas first' order effect.
agent_test: Test an explicit 'list the modal answer, then exclude it' step vs VS vs plain at equal tokens. No direct discard-first-k test exists yet (gap 3 open).

claim: In LLMs divergent breadth and convergent task fulfilment are separable: they correlate weakly; scale and reasoning raise convergent scores but not divergent breadth; temperature raises semantic entropy.
schema_part: two phases: loose generation then control
agent_test: Use separate metrics for each phase (semantic entropy vs task fulfilment). Convergent side is LLM-judged.

claim: On insight-style puzzles with one checkable answer, LLMs fail at the non-obvious connection, not at retrieving facts (factual-vs-creative drop 6-17%); more thinking effort raises accuracy.
agent_test: Add a forced cross-domain linking step; measure on a CresOWLve subset vs added thinking tokens.

claim: A same-model verifier pass with repeated acceptance (5 passes) lifted IMO 2025 accuracy from 21-38% (best of 32) to 85.7% (5 of 6), but this is a checkable task and no verifier accuracy is reported; novelty self-judging stays near chance (K13).
agent_test: Pair a novelty generator with an external check (executed code, retrieval) rather than self-ranking. Not equal tokens.

claim: Executive network activity is present from the start of an idea (above default in early windows, Lloyd-Cox 2022; abstract level), so the generation pass in an agent should not be control-free. Staging evidence is tentative.
agent_test: Compare control-free generate pass vs generate with light constraints at equal tokens.

claim: Human-AI study: users' preferred persona (divergent or convergent coach) often differed from objective performance; fluency did not differ from control.
agent_test: Evaluate steps by outcome, not by self-reported preference.
